  </bpmn:collaboration>

  <bpmn:process id="Process_Producer" name="Chainsaw Production" isExecutable="false">

    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_Properties" name="Customer properties received">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_Properties" messageRef="Msg_Properties"/>
    </bpmn:startEvent>

    <bpmn:parallelGateway id="Gateway_Production_Split" name="Start production"/>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_OrderParts" name="Order parts from various online sources"/>

      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_PartsArrived" messageRef="Msg_PartsArrived_Dummy"/>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>

    <bpmn:manualTask id="ManualTask_Inspect" name="Inspect all parts manually"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_Assemble" name="Assemble chainsaw"/>

    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_Update" name="Send production update to customer">
      <bpmn:standardLoopCharacteristics id="Loop_Update" testBefore="false">
        <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tExpression">production not yet finished</bpmn:conditionExpression>
      </bpmn:standardLoopCharacteristics>
    </bpmn:sendTask>

    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_FirstSaw" name="Send first chainsaw to customer"/>

    <bpmn:eventBasedGateway id="Gateway_Approval" name="Customer decision"/>

    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="IntermediateCatch_Approval" name="Customer likes first chainsaw">

    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>
    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="IntermediateCatch_Rejection" name="Customer does not like first chainsaw">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_Rejection" messageRef="Msg_Rejection"/>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>

    <bpmn:task id="Task_ProduceRest" name="Produce remaining chainsaws of order"/>

    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_RestCompleted" name="Rest of order produced"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_Rejected" name="First chainsaw not accepted"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_UpdatesEnded" name="Production updates ended"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_1" sourceRef="StartEvent_Properties" targetRef="Gateway_Production_Split"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_2" sourceRef="Gateway_Production_Split" targetRef="Task_OrderParts"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_3" sourceRef="Gateway_Production_Split" targetRef="SendTask_Update"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_4" sourceRef="Task_OrderParts" targetRef="IntermediateCatch_PartsArrived"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_5" sourceRef="IntermediateCatch_PartsArrived" targetRef="ManualTask_Inspect"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_6" sourceRef="ManualTask_Inspect" targetRef="Task_Assemble"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_7" sourceRef="Task_Assemble" targetRef="SendTask_FirstSaw"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_8" sourceRef="SendTask_FirstSaw" targetRef="Gateway_Approval"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_9" sourceRef="Gateway_Approval" targetRef="IntermediateCatch_Approval"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_10" sourceRef="Gateway_Approval" targetRef="IntermediateCatch_Rejection"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_11" sourceRef="IntermediateCatch_Approval" targetRef="Task_ProduceRest"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_12" sourceRef="Task_ProduceRest" targetRef="End_RestCompleted"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_13" sourceRef="IntermediateCatch_Rejection" targetRef="End_Rejected"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_14" sourceRef="SendTask_Update" targetRef="End_UpdatesEnded"/>
  </bpmn:process>

</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description states that a later part of the work is carried out only if the receiving party accepts an earlier delivered result, and the description does not state that any step repeats: Model an exclusive gateway after the delivery step. Put the boolean condition on the outgoing sequence flow that continues the remaining work, and write that condition as a conditionExpression that is a direct child of the sequenceFlow element. Never place a conditionExpression inside a loop characteristics element or any other element that does not allow it. Use a loop characteristic only when the description states that a step repeats.
rules.situation: the description states that a later part of the work is carried out only if the receiving party accepts an earlier delivered result, and the description does not state that any step repeats

rules.instruction: When the description states that a party reviews a delivered intermediate result and its positive or negative judgment decides whether further work is carried out: Model the judgment as an exclusive gateway placed after the delivery activity, with one conditional outgoing sequence flow per outcome (for example, approved or rejected) leading to the corresponding continuation. Do not use an event-based gateway for this judgment, because no competing events race each other; the decision is a single evaluated outcome.
rules.situation: the description states that a party reviews a delivered intermediate result and its positive or negative judgment decides whether further work is carried out

rules.instruction: When the description says that after a starting condition is met, a described action is to be carried out in parallel with other actions, and the action is not listed as a step of its own in a later sentence: Model the described action as a task placed on its own branch directly after the parallel split that begins the concurrent work, and keep it on that branch. Do not drop it or fold it into the event that starts the branch, and do not replace it with a waiting event. Fork the concurrent branches from the split with one unconditional flow each.
rules.situation: the description says that after a starting condition is met, a described action is to be carried out in parallel with other actions, and the action is not listed as a step of its own in a later sentence

rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant performs an action such as reviewing or identifying something, and reports its result as a finding within the ongoing flow: Model the stated action as a task performed by that participant, placed in the sequence where the action occurs. Do not replace it with an intermediate catch event named after the finding. Reserve intermediate catch events for occurrences the process waits for, such as a message, signal, timer, or condition.
rules.situation: the description states an action that the company itself performs, such as determining a specification from information it has received or inspecting received items, in a sentence of its own, and that sentence does not state that the process must wait for a message, signal, time, or condition

rules.instruction: When the description states that a person must wait for ordered or awaited items to arrive, and then performs a manual check of those items before a further activity can start, with the check linked to that activity by a 'then' or similar sequence: Model the wait for the items as an intermediate catch event placed after the ordering activity. Place the manual check as a single activity whose incoming sequence flow comes directly from that catch event, and whose outgoing sequence flow leads directly into the next activity that uses the checked items. Do not attach the check to an earlier point, do not route it through a parallel branch that bypasses the arrival, and do not drop the check or merge it into the next activity.
rules.situation: the description states that a person must wait for ordered or awaited items to arrive, and then performs a manual check of those items before a further activity can start, with the check linked to that activity by a 'then' or similar sequence

rules.instruction: When the description names a step that the process owner carries out itself, such as placing an order, determining specifications, or inspecting received material, and a separate waiting period for the outcome of that step follows or runs alongside it: Model the step the owner carries out as its own task, placed in the order the description gives and before any event that waits for its outcome. Model only the waiting for the outcome as an intermediate catch event. Do not replace the owner's step with a start event or a catch event, and do not drop it from the model.
rules.situation: the description names a step that the process owner carries out itself, such as placing an order, determining specifications, or inspecting received material, and a separate waiting period for the outcome of that step follows or runs alongside it
